full_judgment:
2. The aforesaid CR Case arose out of a complaint filed by the complainant Abdul Mazid on 6-12-76 in the Court of the Sub divisional Magistrate Bhola alleging that the accused-petitioners forcibly took away paddy worth Taka 600 on the 19th Agrahayan, 1383 BS corresponding to 5-12-76 from the complainant's portion of the land situated in the northern side of plot No. 15.5 of Khatian No. 79 of Mouza Dewalashipur. The accused-petitioner made out a case that the predecessors-in-interest of the accused-petitioners purchased the entire plot No. 1545 measuring 1.44 acres of land about 40 years ago and since then the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioner and there after the petitioners have been in possession of the entire plot. They grew the paddy in the land and took away the same. The complainant opposite-party procured a fraudulent kabala in respect of 12 decimals of land appertaining to the plot and got his name fraudulently recorded in the SA Khatian for correction of which the accused-petitioners instituted Title Suit No. 648 of 1976 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Bhola, on 13-12-76 which is pending. The learned Magistrate convicted the accused-petitioners under Section 379 of the Bangladesh Penal Code as well as under section 147 BPC and sentenced them to pay a fine of Taka 50 each, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for one month. 

 4. Including the complainant himself, 6 witnesses in all were examined on behalf of the prosecution and one witness was examined on behalf of the defence. Both the parties filed some documents also in support of their respective claim. Mr Shah Mohammad Sharif, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioners contends before me that the documents filed by the accused-petitioners were not considered by both courts below. It appears from the judgment passed in criminal Revision No. 59(3) of 1978 that the learned Additional Sessions Judge took into consideration that the accused-petitioners filed some documents in support of their claim. But the learned Sessions Judge took the view that the accused-petitioners could not thrash out their case by adducing evidence as to how they have been possessing the entire plot by virtue of their deeds. The documents filed by the accused-petitioners did not appear to have been put in evidence as they were exhibited as evidence in the case, either the documents appear to have been filed at the time of examination of the accused-petitioners under section 342 CrPC to form part of the statements of the accused-petitioners made in their examination under section 342 CrPC. As such, the courts below would not have been justified to look into the contents of the documents which are not included in evidence and which do not from part of the statements made by the accused-petitioners under section 342 CrPC. Mr Shah Md Sharif himself admits before me that the documents filed by the defence do not show that the accused-petitioners acquired more than 1.20 acres of land out of 1.44 acres in the Dag. The registered Kabala filed by the complainant which was executed on 6-4-75 shows that Abdul Mannan and Md. Arshed, the 2 sons of the complainant Abdul Mazid purchased 12 decimals of land from one Ali Ahmed and another Kuti Mia, the sons of Ibrahim Molla. The name of the complainant Abdul Mazid is recorded in SA Khatian as having 4 gandas 3 koras 7 tills share in the disputed dag. The petition of complaint was filed on 6-12-76 but the Title suit No. 648 of 1976 was instituted by the complainant on 13-12 76. So no importance should be given about the institution of the title suit. But the petitioners have not got documents to show acquisition of the entire lands of the dag by the accused-petitioners. It is not unlikely that the complainant might grow paddy on some portion of a registered Kabala shows that he purchased some portion out of the dag in the name of his sons. But some other consideration led me to take the view that the order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Magistrate cannot be upheld.
